attacks.claim: The PR says startup fails if the secret is missing or short, but the diff never constructs Settings at boot. The route resolves it lazily via Depends(get_settings), so a bad secret would more likely surface as a 500 on webhook requests. No test covers the startup failure.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: eager Settings construction or startup hook; PR text "startup fails if it is missing or short" vs. "settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)"

attacks.claim: VOLTLOG_PLUGCLOUD_SECRET is a required field with no default, and the diff adds no preflight check, example .env change, or upgrade-order guidance. Any operator who upgrades without the secret gets a broken instance. Vendor-side signing configuration is also not sequenced with the upgrade.
attacks.evidence: "plugcloud_secret: SecretStr" (no default); ABSENT: changes to the compose .env template, example env file, release notes, or vendor-configuration sequencing

attacks.claim: Signature enforcement goes live immediately with no shadow or log-only mode and no documented rollback. A wrong secret or a wrong header assumption rejects every reading with 401 at once, and readings dropped in that gap are not recoverable.
attacks.evidence: "returns a bare 401 on any failure"; ABSENT: staged rollout, shadow-verification mode, or rollback plan for the enforcement switch

attacks.claim: Rejections are logged only at warning level, with no counter, metric, or alert. A misconfigured secret silently refuses all readings and looks the same as an attack, so the operator has no reliable signal.
attacks.evidence: log.warning("plugcloud webhook rejected: %s", exc); ABSENT: metric, alert threshold, or runbook entry for 401 spikes

attacks.claim: Making plugcloud_secret required with no default will break any other code path that builds Settings (CLI, migrations, scripts, other tests). Only tests/conftest.py is updated, and the diff shows no audit of other call sites.
attacks.evidence: "plugcloud_secret: SecretStr" (no default); the only construction updated is "return Settings(database_url=TEST_DB_URL, plugcloud_secret=\"t\" * 32)"; ABSENT: list of other Settings(...) call sites

attacks.claim: The handler buffers the full request body with await request.body() before any authentication. The app sets no size bound, so the 1 MB cap relies entirely on the reverse proxy.
attacks.evidence: body = await request.body() precedes signing.verify(...); "the reverse proxy caps request bodies at 1 MB"; ABSENT: in-app max body size

attacks.claim: A captured valid delivery can be replayed anywhere in the 5-minute tolerance window, since nothing binds a delivery to a nonce or ID. A replayed older batch could overwrite a later correction, because upserts key on (device_id, measured_at).
attacks.evidence: if abs(current - int(timestamp)) > TOLERANCE_SECONDS: raise SignatureError(...) (no nonce or delivery-ID check in signing.verify); "Readings are already upserted by (device_id, measured_at)"

attacks.claim: There is one signing secret and no rotation overlap. Rotating it requires vendor and operator to switch simultaneously, and any mismatch causes a rejection window with no fallback key.
attacks.evidence: plugcloud_secret: SecretStr (single value); ABSENT: rotation procedure or dual-secret acceptance

attacks.claim: The secret validator checks only length (at least 32 characters), not entropy, so a weak 32-character value passes.
attacks.evidence: if len(v.get_secret_value()) < 32: raise ValueError("must be at least 32 characters")

attacks.claim: The PR description says the endpoint returns a bare 401, but the code returns a JSON detail body. The description and the contract disagree.
attacks.evidence: "returns a bare 401 on any failure" vs. raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="invalid signature")

attacks.claim: The validator error message does not name the environment variable. An operator seeing a pydantic error about plugcloud_secret has to map it to VOLTLOG_PLUGCLOUD_SECRET by hand.
attacks.evidence: raise ValueError("must be at least 32 characters")
